teaching.hint: Which early position could be made smaller while still breaking its mirror match?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Lexicographic minimization favors the earliest possible decrease, but changing the center of an odd-length palindrome cannot break symmetry.
solution_outline.approach: For length one, return empty. Scan the first half for the first character above a and replace it with a. If none exists, replace the final character with b.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before finding a non-a character in the first half, no earlier position admits a lowering edit that breaks the palindrome. The untouched mirrored character ensures any such first-half lowering does break it.
solution_outline.correctness: A first-half non-a character can be lowered to the smallest letter and becomes unequal to its unchanged mirror; the earliest such position makes the lexicographically smallest possible valid result. If no such position exists, every first-half character is already a and the only lowerable possible middle position cannot break symmetry, so the least harmful valid increase is b at the final position. A length-one string can never become non-palindromic.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for a returned copy of the n-character string, with O(1) extra space beyond that copy.
solution_outline.pitfall: Changing the middle character of an odd-length palindrome leaves it a palindrome, even if the string becomes lexicographically smaller.

common_wrong_turns: Edit the middle character of an odd-length string
Return a character for a length-one input
source_fidelity_notes: The multiple-option source example was removed; exactly-one replacement, lowercase alphabet, minimum lexicographic result, length-one impossibility, and bounds were retained.
